parsed.explanation: Thin-data, small jurisdiction. Structural signals: no trans-specific criminalisation, no facility restrictions, same-sex conduct legal, foreign documents accepted (visitor unaffected by the absent marker-change regime), functioning European-style rule of law. The 2012 account describes a comfortable, low-hostility society with 'few organized enemies'; marriage/adoption equality (2025) marks an improving trajectory. Negatives: no gender-identity anti-discrimination ground (a resident gap, not visitor exposure), dated official hostility from the head of state (2016/2021 remarks, partly superseded), Catholic state religion, and no documented enforcement record either way. No documented targeting of trans people, no facility/custody exposures; the dossier's worst feature is tier-5 paper-gap uncertainty plus dated disapproval — friction, not hostility. Extrapolating from rule-of-law governance and no enforcement history resolves above elevated risk; without documented protections actually operating for trans visitors, it sits below the 0.85 tier.
